scope: CANTOS and CIRT as summarised in a stored review abstract on residual cardiovascular risk.

keyRecommendations.text: CANTOS enrolled patients with prior myocardial infarction and hsCRP at least 2 mg/L and reported a 15% MACE reduction with canakinumab (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74–0.98).
CIRT was stopped early for lack of benefit of low-dose methotrexate on MACE in coronary disease with type 2 diabetes or the metabolic syndrome.
keyRecommendations.population: Stable coronary disease with diabetes or metabolic syndrome

clinicalBottomLine: Canakinumab reduced MACE in CANTOS; low-dose methotrexate did not show MACE benefit in CIRT and that trial stopped early.
notableCaveats: Canakinumab dose and fatal-infection counts are not in this abstract and are not asked. COLCOT is in the same abstract but is not one of the named trials in the topic.
